docs.title: TM1 REST API Documentation
docs.text: The TM1 REST API lets you manage and query IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) programmatically over HTTP — provision databases, model dimensions and cubes, read and write cell data, run MDX, and execute processes.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "https://<host>/api/v1/Authenticate" \
  -u "$TM1_USER:$TM1_PASSWORD" \
  | jq -r .AccessToken)

curl "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

See First Request for the full walkthrough, including creating your first database.

docs.title: Databases API
docs.text:
Endpoints for creating, listing, inspecting, and deleting TM1 databases. See Databases for a conceptual overview.

Note

Every request below requires a valid Authorization header. See Authentication.

docs.title: Create a database
docs.text:
Creates a new, empty database and starts provisioning it.

POST /api/v1/Databases

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description Name string Yes Unique name for the database. Letters, numbers, and underscores only. Type string No Database type, e.g. Standard. Defaults to Standard if omitted. curlPython 
curl -X POST "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "Name": "SalesPlanning"
      }'

import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    json={"Name": "SalesPlanning"},
)
response.raise_for_status()
database = response.json()

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
201 Created on success, with the new database in the response body and a Location header pointing at it.

{
  "Name": "SalesPlanning",
  "Type": "Standard",
  "State": "Provisioning"
}

Provisioning happens asynchronously — poll Get a database until State is Running before sending it any other requests.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Meaning 400 Bad Request Name is missing, malformed, or uses reserved characters. 401 Unauthorized The bearer token is missing, expired, or invalid. 409 Conflict A database with that name already exists.

docs.title: List databases
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/Databases

curl "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Returns an array of database objects in the same shape as Create a database.

docs.title: Get a database
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/Databases('{name}')

curl "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Returns 404 Not Found if no database with that name exists.

docs.title: Delete a database
docs.text:
DELETE /api/v1/Databases('{name}')

curl -X DELETE "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Returns 204 No Content on success. This permanently removes the database and all of its cubes, dimensions, and data — the operation cannot be undone.

docs.title: Dimensions API
docs.text:
Endpoints for creating, listing, inspecting, and deleting dimensions within a database. See Dimensions for a conceptual overview.

Note

Every request below requires a valid Authorization header. See Authentication.

docs.title: Create a dimension
docs.text:
Creates a dimension, its default hierarchy, and any leaf elements you supply, in one call.

POST /api/v1/Databases('{database}')/Dimensions

docs.title: Request body
Response
docs.text:
201 Created on success, with the new dimension in the response body.

{
  "Name": "Region",
  "Hierarchies": [
    {
      "Name": "Region",
      "Elements": [
        { "Name": "North", "Type": "Numeric" },
        { "Name": "South", "Type": "Numeric" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Meaning 400 Bad Request Name is missing, or an element has an invalid Type. 401 Unauthorized The bearer token is missing, expired, or invalid. 404 Not Found The database in the URL doesn't exist. 409 Conflict A dimension with that name already exists.

docs.title: Adding a consolidated element
docs.text:
Consolidations are added as edges between a parent and child element in a hierarchy, after both elements exist:

POST /api/v1/Databases('{database}')/Dimensions('{dimension}')/Hierarchies('{hierarchy}')/Edges

curl -X POST "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')/Dimensions('Region')/Hierarchies('Region')/Edges" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "ParentName": "Total Region",
        "ComponentName": "North",
        "Weight": 1
      }'

Total Region must already exist as an element with Type: "Consolidated" before you can add children to it.

docs.title: List dimensions
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/Databases('{database}')/Dimensions

curl "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')/Dimensions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Returns an array of dimension objects in the same shape as Create a dimension.

docs.title: Get a dimension
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/Databases('{database}')/Dimensions('{name}')

curl "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')/Dimensions('Region')" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Returns 404 Not Found if no dimension with that name exists in the database.

docs.title: Delete a dimension
docs.text:
DELETE /api/v1/Databases('{database}')/Dimensions('{name}')

curl -X DELETE "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')/Dimensions('Region')" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Returns 204 No Content on success.

Warning

A dimension can't be deleted while it's still in use by a cube. Remove it from any cubes first.

docs.title: Databases
docs.text:
A database is the top-level container in TM1 / IBM Planning Analytics. It's a single, independently managed TM1 instance that holds its own cubes, dimensions, processes, and data — comparable to what earlier TM1 documentation called a "server" or "model."

Everything else in this API — dimensions, cubes, views, cellsets, and cells — lives inside a database and is addressed relative to it.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
A database goes through a small number of states as it's provisioned and torn down:

State Meaning Provisioning The database has been requested and infrastructure is being allocated. Running The database is available and accepting requests. Stopped The database exists but is not currently running. Deleting The database has been marked for deletion and is being removed.

You create a database once and then interact with it repeatedly through the Databases API and the object APIs scoped underneath it.

docs.title: Addressing a database
docs.text:
Once a database exists, requests to objects inside it are scoped by the database name in the URL path, e.g.:

/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')/Cubes

See Creating a database for how to provision one, and First Request for a walkthrough of calling the API end to end.

docs.title: Dimensions
docs.text: A dimension defines one axis of a cube — for example Time, Region, or Product. Every cube is built from an ordered list of dimensions, so a dimension must exist before it can be referenced when creating a cube.

docs.title: Elements
docs.text:
A dimension is made up of elements — the individual members you can slice data by. Each element has a type:

Type Meaning Numeric A leaf element that stores numeric values, e.g. North, South. String A leaf element that stores text values. Consolidated A parent element that aggregates other elements (its children), e.g. Total Region rolling up North + South.

Consolidated elements don't store data directly — their value is derived by summing (or otherwise aggregating) their children.

docs.title: Hierarchies
docs.text:
Elements live inside a hierarchy, and a dimension can contain more than one. Every dimension has a default hierarchy with the same name as the dimension itself; additional hierarchies let you expose alternate rollups of the same elements (e.g. a Region dimension with both a geographic hierarchy and a sales-org hierarchy) without duplicating them.

Consolidations — which elements roll up into which — are defined as edges between a parent element and a child element within a hierarchy, not as a property of the element itself.

docs.title: Relationship to cubes
docs.text: A cube's shape is defined entirely by the dimensions assigned to it, in order. Before creating a cube, make sure every dimension it needs already exists — see Creating a dimension.

docs.title: Addressing a dimension
docs.text:
Dimensions are scoped under a database:

/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')/Dimensions('Region')

And a hierarchy is scoped under its dimension:

/api/v1/Databases('SalesPlanning')/Dimensions('Region')/Hierarchies('Region')

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every request to the TM1 REST API must include a bearer token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

Requests without a valid token — or with an expired one — receive 401 Unauthorized.

docs.title: Obtaining a token
docs.text:
Exchange your username and password for a token by calling the authentication endpoint with HTTP Basic credentials:

POST /api/v1/Authenticate
curlPython 
curl -X POST "https://<host>/api/v1/Authenticate" \
  -u "$TM1_USER:$TM1_PASSWORD"

import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://<host>/api/v1/Authenticate",
    auth=(username, password),
)
response.raise_for_status()
token = response.json()["AccessToken"]

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "AccessToken": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "ExpiresIn": 3600
}

AccessToken is the value you send as the bearer token; ExpiresIn is its lifetime in seconds.

docs.title: Using the token
docs.text:
Attach the token to every subsequent request:

curl "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

The examples throughout this documentation assume $TOKEN (or, in Python, a token variable) holds a valid access token obtained this way.

docs.title: Token expiry
docs.text:
Tokens expire after ExpiresIn seconds. Once a token expires, requests fail with 401 Unauthorized — re-authenticate to obtain a new one rather than trying to refresh it in place.

Tip

Don't re-authenticate on every request. Cache the token and its expiry, and only fetch a new one when it's close to expiring or a request comes back 401.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Meaning 400 Bad Request The request is missing credentials or is malformed. 401 Unauthorized The username or password is incorrect. 429 Too Many Requests Too many authentication attempts in a short period. Back off before retrying.

Warning

Never hard-code credentials or tokens in source control. Load them from environment variables or a secrets manager, as shown in the examples above.

docs.title: First Request
docs.text: This walks through calling the TM1 REST API end to end: authenticate, make a read-only request, then create your first database.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The hostname of your TM1 / Planning Analytics environment (<host> below).
  • A username and password with access to it.

docs.title: Step 1: Authenticate
docs.text:
Exchange your credentials for a bearer token, as described in Authentication:

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "https://<host>/api/v1/Authenticate" \
  -u "$TM1_USER:$TM1_PASSWORD" \
  | jq -r .AccessToken)

Every request from here on sends this token in the Authorization header.

docs.title: Step 2: Make a read-only request
docs.text:
Confirm everything is working by listing the databases you already have access to:

curlPython 
curl "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://<host>/api/v1/Authenticate",
    auth=(username, password),
)
response.raise_for_status()
token = response.json()["AccessToken"]

response = requests.get(
    "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(response.json())

A successful response is 200 OK with a JSON array — empty if you haven't created any databases yet.

docs.title: Step 3: Create your first database
docs.text:
Now create one, per Create a database:

curl -X POST "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "Name": "GettingStarted" }'

The response comes back 201 Created with "State": "Provisioning". Poll it until it's ready:

curl "https://<host>/api/v1/Databases('GettingStarted')" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Once State is "Running", the database is ready to hold dimensions and cubes.

docs.text:

  • Dimensions — build the axes your cubes will use.
  • Authentication — token expiry and error handling.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: The TM1 REST API lets you manage and query IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) programmatically over HTTP. Anything you can do in the TM1 client tools — create a database, define dimensions and cubes, read or write cell data, run MDX queries, execute processes — you can also do with a plain HTTP request.

docs.title: What you can do with it
docs.text:
• Provision and manage databases — create, inspect, and delete TM1 databases.
  • Model data — define dimensions, cubes, and their structure.
  • Read and write data — query and update cells through views and cellsets.
  • Run logic — execute MDX queries and TI processes against your data.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
The API follows OData v4 conventions:

  • Base URL — every endpoint is rooted at https://<host>/api/v1/.
  • JSON — requests and responses use application/json.
  • Entity addressing — named entities are addressed with single quotes inside parentheses, e.g. Databases('SalesPlanning'), Dimensions('Region').
  • Nesting — child resources are addressed by chaining paths, e.g. Databases('SalesPlanning')/Dimensions('Region')/Hierarchies('Region').
  • Standard HTTP verbs — GET to read, POST to create, PATCH to update, DELETE to remove.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
To follow along with this documentation you'll need:

  • Access to a TM1 / Planning Analytics environment and its hostname.
  • A username and password (or other credentials) authorized against it.

docs.text:

  • Concepts — what each object (database, dimension, cube, ...) is and how they relate.
  • API Reference — endpoint-by-endpoint request/response detail.
  • Tutorials — task-oriented walkthroughs, like reading or writing cube data.
